newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close weak, but above lows.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close weak, but above lows.

text.p: Short covering lifted CME lumber futures from a near limit loss in September early but the market remained under pressure from weak cash lumber prices, traders said.
Lumber closed $7.50 to $0.30 per thousand board feet lower with July off $5.30 at $369.20 per tbf and September off $7.00 at $364.30 per tbf after being down to $362.00 early.
Falling cash lumber prices weighed on futures which triggered sell stops in early trading. Secondaries have been offering spruce at discounts to mill levels in order to move stocks, traders said.

Cash sources noted some mills were also taking lower counter offers. Most indications put spruce in the $355 to $360 per tbf area, below the official Random Lengths quote of $362 late last week. Also, some talk circulated of sales under the $355 level, sources said.
Technically the market is also looking weak and poised to move lower on Wednesday, traders said.
September closed below its 20-day moving average and stochastics rolled over into a sell, they added.
